content_map.problem: The actual state of a distributed system can continuously diverge from what operators declared, so one successful command does not prove that the intended condition remains true.
content_map.thesis: Controllers are non-terminating control loops that observe current state and make or request changes so the system moves toward desired state.
mechanisms: watch a resource specification expressing desired state
make or request a bounded corrective change
examples: Job controller creates/manages Pods to move a Job toward completion
controllers may manage external systems such as node capacity directly
claims: Kubernetes controllers are control loops that watch cluster state and make/request changes where needed.
A resource spec represents desired state and controllers work to bring current state closer to it.
Kubernetes uses many controllers managing particular aspects of state rather than one monolithic control loop.
The overall cluster does not need to become permanently stable for controllers to remain useful.
evidence: Official Controllers documentation defines the thermostat-style control-loop analogy and desired/current-state comparison.
The Job controller example shows API-mediated creation/removal of Pods rather than the controller running containers itself.
The design section explicitly favors simple controllers managing particular aspects of cluster state.
assumptions: Desired state is meaningful and sufficiently specified.
Controllers can observe enough current state to decide whether action is required.
Corrective actions are designed so repeated reconciliation does not create uncontrolled duplicate side effects.
limitations: The page is conceptual documentation rather than a controller implementation guide.
Reconciliation does not automatically make external side effects idempotent or correct.
Multiple focused controllers can still interact through shared resources and require careful ownership semantics.
open_questions: Which controller-runtime queue/backoff patterns best prevent hot loops and duplicate work?
When should a business process be modeled as reconciliation versus a durable workflow execution?

selection.requested_focus: Understand reconciliation/control loops: desired state vs current state, why many small controllers are preferable to one monolith, and what this teaches about resilient automation.
coherent_core: desired state is distinct from observed reality
the controller repeatedly compares the two
actions reduce the delta rather than permanently complete the system
focused controllers compose around bounded responsibilities
drop_notes: Do not expand into general Kubernetes scheduling/networking concepts not required for the controller mental model.
Do not reinterpret preliminary Temporal/controlled-execution retrieval matches as the same concept; they describe different responsibilities.
connections: reconciliation is complementary to durable workflow execution but not equivalent
repeated corrective actions make safe duplicate handling an implementation concern
